content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Research addresses soil moisture sensing technologies, including capacitive probe design and deployment strategies for field-scale crop water management.","sources":[{"id":"R0662","field":"bio","quote":"holds a granted patent for a multi-depth capacitive soil moisture probe"},{"id":"R0662","field":"keywords","quote":"soil moisture sensors"}]},{"text":"Work integrates wireless sensor networks with decision support systems to automate irrigation scheduling while minimizing data collection labor and cost.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07496","field":"abstract","quote":"integrating a network of capacitive soil moisture sensor nodes with a cloud-based irrigation decision support engine"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-07496","field":"abstract","quote":"Automated scheduling reduced irrigation labour time by approximately 85%"}]},{"text":"Research evaluates cost-scalability trade-offs across sensor technologies and develops low-cost IoT alternatives applicable to smallholder and larger operations.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07499","field":"abstract","quote":"suitability for smallholder versus large commercial operations"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-07499","field":"abstract","quote":"research agenda prioritising low-cost IoT sensor integration"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher directly addresses the core challenge of expensive soil moisture sensing through design of multi-depth capacitive probes [R0662], development of wireless IoT sensor networks that reduce deployment and labor costs [SYN-PUB-07496], and evaluation of cost-scalability trade-offs for field-scale monitoring [SYN-PUB-07499], including explicit analysis of sensor placement strategies for diverse farm sizes."}
